newsitem.title: CROATIA: Pliva leads trade in mixed Croatian market.
newsitem.headline: Pliva leads trade in mixed Croatian market.

text.p: Croatian market heavyweight Pliva took the spotlight on Wednesday in a mixed market which saw little increase in turnover from yesterday.

The leading drugs firm was the most active issue, adding six kuna to 499 and selling 7,785 shares. Traders said interest was spurred by arbitrage as brokers sought to profit from a marginal difference in Pliva's price in Zagreb and London.
Its GDRs opened at $16.15 and rose to $16.575 by mid afternoon.
The other Croatian leading company listed abroad, Zagrebacka Banka, fell 20 kuna to 1,980, on volume of 901 shares in what one trader said was investors' saturation with the stock.
"There is nothing new on Zagrebacka to move its price up," a trader at I.C.F. brokerage said.
But the banks' 3E-series preference stock continued to close in on the regular issue, as traders had predicted, adding 30 kuna to 1,400. It traded 646 shares.
The biggest gainer was brewery Karlovacka Pivovara, which added 20 kuna (4.5 percent) to 460, on volume of 608 shares.
"Karlovacka is a sort of a hot-stock at the moment," the source said. "There is plenty of room for it to grow."
Another trader said he expected it to grow up to around 600 kuna in the next few months. It is more than 60-percent owned by a Chilean group Cervecerias Unidas.
"Karlovacka is a very solid firm, it has plans to expand and is owned and run by a foreign company, which all contributes to an increase in investors' interest," said Zoran Ilic of Consult Invest.
He singled out hotelier Plava Laguna which reached 1,500 kuna on volume of 925 as the most interesting development of the day.

"Not only the price but also the volume indicates that Laguna could gain some more in the next few days," Ilic said, adding that market expectations ahead of the shareholders' meeting, scheduled for July 4, were high.
Of other hoteliers, Istraturist lost one kuna to 180 on an exceptionally high volume of 2,100 shares. Arenaturist lost five kuna to 125 and Riviera remained flat at 145, both on smaller volumes.
Of other intensely traded stocks, food concern Podravka sold 3,039 shares, losing two kuna to 273.
Ordinary shares of fully-listed Varazdinska Banka added six kuna to 210, trading 1,758 shares.
The biggest decliner was textile firm Varteks, which lost eight kuna to close at 65, with 121 shares sold.
Seven of 15 active issues rose, seven fell and one was flat. Volume was slightly lower at 19,690 units, turnover higher at 10.3 million kuna.
